clinician.final_diagnosis: myasthenic crisis requiring intubation and ventilator support
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension presented with acute onset dysphagia, nasal speech, and bulbar weakness post mild COVID-19. Serological testing showed elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies and repeat nerve stimulation revealed significant decremental responses, confirming myasthenia gravis. Negative MuSK antibody and normal brain/spinal MRI were documented. The patient exhibited marked improvement with intravenous neostigmine. Eight days into admission, he developed neck and respiratory muscle weakness with type II respiratory failure, necessitating intubation and ventilator support, consistent with a myasthenic crisis.
